sections.value:
F222 — PID17600 CPU attribution, measurement-only

Conclusion: CPU-time slope confirms about 32% of one core on dba0c0803b. Both samples place the largest observed non-wait subsystem in SQLite workers; both also directly identify GET /v1/seats -> SqliteStatus::read row/decode/drop work. They do NOT identify which HTTP route submitted each asynchronous SQL query. No single route can honestly be named as owning all daemon CPU without request/SQL correlation.

## Measurement and CPU slope
Same PID17600, launch 2026-11-19 17:53:30 +1000 and commit dba0c0803b throughout. Window: 08:22:18.466856Z–08:26:14.443383Z, elapsed 235.976 s; CPU time 9:26.05→10:41.23, delta 75.18 s = 31.86% of one core. This is measured TIME slope, not ps's moving %CPU snapshot. Includes one of the diagnostic samples and four ping reads; not a controlled idle trial.

| UTC reading | Accumulated CPU TIME | Interval wall s | Interval CPU s | One-core slope |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 08:22:18.466856 | 9:26.05 | — | — | — |
| 08:23:41.899849 | 9:52.48 | 83.433 | 26.43 | 31.68% |
| 08:25:01.328266 | 10:17.32 | 79.428 | 24.84 | 31.27% |
| 08:26:14.443383 | 10:41.23 | 73.115 | 23.91 | 32.70% |

## Two spaced 5-second call-tree captures
Commands: /usr/bin/sample 17600 5 -file /tmp/f222-sample-1.txt, then the same command with sample-2. Capture starts: 08:22:13.227Z and 08:25:40.700Z, 207.473 s apart. Both completed before parent released the bounce hold. Raw files retained at those paths; hashes and parsed summaries embedded in evidence and /tmp/f222-cpu-counters.json.

The table sums exclusive leaf sample weights into mutually exclusive subsystem buckets, excluding named blocking wait syscalls. It is an occupancy/CPU-or-IO proxy, NOT CPU percentage, request count, call count or latency. pread/open can themselves wait for IO. Parked runtime threads dominate the raw all-thread report and are not CPU culprits.

| Sampled subsystem / call tree | Non-wait leaves, sample 1 | Non-wait leaves, sample 2 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| SQLx SQLite connection workers -> sqlite3_step/Btree/Vdbe/row-value allocation | 442 | 471 |
| HTTP seats -> SqliteStatus::read -> SQLx row decode/drop | 95 | 105 |
| double_seat::live_claude_records -> claude_session_records -> filesystem open | 90 | 25 |
| PaneObserver::start -> tap attach verification / drain / capture | 32 | 36 |
| Other non-wait locations | 147 | 165 |

Direct stack anchors: sample1:161-197,350-410,1896-1955 show seats/status work; sample2:168-225,465-517,1899-1965 repeats it. SQLx worker trees and sqlite3_step occur across four worker threads in each capture. sample1:3642-3652,3664-3674,3706-3716,3735-3745 show four concurrent Claude census workers; 88 of that subsystem's first-capture leaves end in open. sample2:2974,3026,3050 show it again. Pane observer's inclusive 308/301 samples include 276/265 known wait leaves: chiefly ControlClient::ask -> recv_timeout/semaphore_timedwait. Those waits are not evidence that pane observation consumes that much daemon CPU; tmux server execution is outside PID17600.

## Counters / request rate visibility
No generic per-route request count, /metrics route, or successful-request access log is exposed by this build. Health only exposes spawns, registration attempts and cache-sidecar counters. Endpoint::ALL/path (http/mod.rs:259-394), require_bearer (:788-827), Health (:829-890) and serve.rs have no route-count layer. The sidecar's requests counter is NOT daemon HTTP traffic and is not substituted.

Across the same 235.976 s, daemon spawns 691→722 (+31, 0.1314/s): git.community +14, ddocs.community +10, tmux.rename-window +4, ps.registration-native-process +2, gh.delivered +1; every other recorded site +0. Registration attempts 80→81: explicit.pane.unchanged +1, paying two ps reads; receive/native attempts +0. The whole-window CPU is therefore not explained by a storm of new native registrations, nor by hundreds of daemon child launches/s. Counters do not quantify other in-process work. Full before/after by-op/by-key values are embedded.

## Four sample-backed optimization candidates and scaling
Rates below are SOURCE-CONFIGURED/FORMULAE, not measured arrivals. N is distinct live tracked panes; S is all durable seat rows, including tombstoned rows; F is Claude session-record files; R is seats-route arrivals/s and U is unowned-pane diagnostic arrivals/s, both unavailable.

1. GET /v1/seats status projection: R × S correlated status work, descriptor decoding and dropping, then filtering. http/mod.rs:4260-4303 calls status.read(None) before tombstone/here/harness/folder/parent filters; store/status.rs:16-36,107-145 selects all seats, latest spine facts and assignment states, then materializes every row. Sample directly proves this path is present. Cuttable: move route-appropriate filters ahead of the expensive projection and avoid full status projection for consumers needing identity-only roster. Cacheable: a mutation-generation-invalidated status projection, preserving single-snapshot badge/assignment-close semantics. No broad TTL cache that can return stale authority/ownership. Federation defaults to one request per peer per response+1 s (core/config.rs:214; federation/fanin.rs); configured peers/actual R not observed.

2. Rechecking healthy tap ownership: default 600 ms observer => two control-client reads per pane per tick for marker and pane_pipe, capacity 3.33N reads/s. pane_observer.rs:347-382; tmux/lib.rs:1129-1164. Sample includes attach_pane_tap/tap_marker. Cuttable: include the same fresh pipe/marker facts in the existing all-pane snapshot rather than two extra round trips per pane. Preserve detection of externally detached/replaced taps; an unvalidated tracked=true cache is unsafe.

3. Per-pane capture/drain and full descriptor roster: default observer capacity 1.67 ticks/s; one capture and two tap metadata/drains per pane => 1.67N captures/s plus 3.33N metadata checks/s, and one live-roster query per tick. pane_observer.rs:227-246,384-408; tmux/lib.rs:1264-1298. Together with tap verification the tmux read capacity is about 5N/s (675/s if the reported 135 seats were 135 distinct tracked healthy panes; that condition was NOT measured). Capture reply copy/join and composer scan can be reduced; narrow observer roster to pane IDs rather than decoding complete descriptors. Do not remove the bracketing drain: trailing bytes prevent stale blank captures from authorizing delivery. MissedTickBehavior::Delay means actual throughput can be lower than these configured capacities.

4. Claude session census on unowned-pane refusal: U × F file reads/parses, with no configured standalone timer in this path. double_seat.rs:125-159 and harnesses/proc.rs:456-474 read every session JSON before filtering to one pane; identity.rs:1453-1459 and fyi.rs:424-436 trigger this only when no live seat owns the pane. Sample shows concurrent repeated census work, but not which caller or request rate. Cuttable/cacheable: coalesce in-flight whole-census scans, or use a bounded invalidated diagnostic snapshot/index; preserve exact pid+start and conservative double-seat refusal. Do not bypass the guard or treat unknown as permission.

## Limits and next diagnostic
These observations justify prioritizing SQL/status projection and repeated census/tmux work; they do not prove a specific commit caused the regression or that any proposed change recovers the 20% bar. Per-route counters plus request-correlated SQL timing are the missing evidence for allocating async worker CPU to callers. Recommend those as a separately owned change, not code in F222. No builds, tests, process restarts, daemon bounce, configuration edits, credential reads or source edits performed. Only the two requested one-off samples, ps/ping readings and source inspection. magicWand: one built-in performance receipt combining CPU-time slope, by-route counts and SQL attribution; current launch counters correctly expose that process count alone misses this CPU cost.
